items.title: WebP Decompression & JPG Re-encoding
items.description: WebP's VP8/VP9 compressed data is fully decompressed, then re-encoded using JPG's DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) compression for maximum compatibility.

items.title: Quality Considerations
items.description: If original WebP was lossy, converting to JPG preserves current quality but cannot restore lost data. Lossless WebP converts to JPG with minimal quality loss (JPG is always lossy).

items.title: Transparency Loss
items.description: JPG doesn't support transparency. WebP's alpha channel is removed during conversion, with transparent areas filled with solid color (typically white or black).

items.title: Maximum Compatibility
items.description: JPG has 100% universal support across all browsers (since 1995), email clients, social media, print software, and devices. The safest format for guaranteed compatibility.

items.title: Email Marketing & Newsletters
items.description: Ensure images display in all email clients.
items.content: Convert WebP to JPG for email campaigns and newsletters. Many email clients don't support WebP (Outlook, Apple Mail, Gmail). JPG ensures universal display. Use quality 85-90 for good balance. Essential for transactional emails, marketing campaigns, and email signatures. JPG is the only safe choice for email images.

items.title: Social Media & Sharing
items.content: Convert WebP to JPG for social media uploads. While major platforms support WebP, JPG ensures compatibility across all platforms and older app versions. Use quality 85-90 for social media. Essential for profile pictures, cover photos, and shared content. JPG is universally supported and processes faster on some platforms.

items.title: Legacy System Support
items.description: Compatibility with older browsers and software.
items.content: Convert WebP to JPG for systems running older browsers (IE11, Safari <14, Chrome <85). Essential for enterprise environments, government websites, and applications targeting older devices. JPG has 100% browser support since 1995. If your analytics show >5% users on old browsers, provide JPG instead of WebP.

items.title: Print & Professional Use
items.description: Prepare images for print and professional applications.
items.content: Convert WebP to JPG for print workflows. Most print software expects JPG, TIFF, or PNG. JPG is the standard for photo printing and professional applications. Use quality 90-95 for print. Essential for brochures, business cards, posters, and professional printing. Start with highest quality WebP available.

items.title: Design Deliverables
items.description: Client deliverables and universal file sharing.
items.content: Convert WebP to JPG for client deliverables and file sharing. JPG is universally recognized and opens in all software without plugins. Use quality 85-95 depending on use case. Essential for design handoffs, client presentations, and file sharing where recipient's software is unknown. JPG is the safe default.

items.title: When to Keep WebP
items.description: Scenarios where WebP is the better choice.
items.content: Keep WebP if: 1) Targeting modern browsers only (95%+ support), 2) Web performance is critical (25-35% smaller than JPG), 3) Need transparency (JPG doesn't support it), 4) Using progressive enhancement (WebP → JPG fallback). WebP excels for modern web apps. Use JPG for emails, print, legacy systems, and universal compatibility.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about WebP to JPG conversion

items.question: Why convert WebP to JPG if WebP is better?
items.answer: Convert WebP to JPG for universal compatibility. While WebP has 95%+ browser support, JPG has 100% support across all browsers (since 1995), email clients, social media, print software, and devices. JPG is essential for emails, print workflows, older browsers, and scenarios where guaranteed compatibility matters more than file size.

items.question: Will converting WebP to JPG affect image quality?
items.answer: Quality depends on the original WebP: 1) Lossy WebP → JPG: Current quality preserved, no additional loss if using high JPG quality (85-95). 2) Lossless WebP → JPG: Slight quality loss since JPG is always lossy, but typically imperceptible at quality 90-95. Use highest JPG quality setting for best results.

items.question: What happens to transparency when converting WebP to JPG?
items.answer: JPG doesn't support transparency. During conversion, transparent areas are filled with a solid background color (typically white or black). If your WebP has transparency, consider converting to PNG instead to preserve it. For photos without important transparency, JPG is fine and results in smaller files than PNG.

items.question: How do file sizes compare between WebP and JPG?
items.answer: WebP is typically 25-35% smaller than JPG at equivalent quality. Converting WebP to JPG will increase file size. For example, a 500KB WebP might become 650-750KB as JPG. This size increase is the tradeoff for universal compatibility. JPG's larger size is acceptable for emails, print, and scenarios where compatibility is critical.

items.question: Which browsers and software support JPG format?
items.answer: JPG has 100% universal support. Supported by all browsers since 1995, all email clients, all social media platforms, all design software, all operating systems, and all image viewers. JPG is the most compatible image format ever created. It's the safe choice when you need guaranteed compatibility across all platforms and devices.

items.question: Is WebP to JPG conversion free and secure?
items.answer: Yes, our WebP to JPG converter is completely free with no registration, watermarks, or payment required. All conversion happens locally in your browser using WebAssembly - your images never leave your device. This ensures 100% privacy and security, with no server uploads, data collection, or third-party access. WebP decoding and JPG encoding are performed entirely client-side.
